new_entities.name: Teen dating violence prevention
new_entities.description: Programs designed to reduce adolescent dating violence perpetration or victimization through school or youth interventions.

edges.effect_quant: A 2022 meta-analysis of 18 trials involving 22,781 adolescents found that dating violence prevention programs reduced combined physical and sexual dating violence outcomes overall (OR 0.78, 95% CI 0.69-0.89), with stronger evidence for physical than sexual violence outcomes.
edges.population: adolescents participating in school-based or youth-targeted dating violence prevention programs
edges.mechanism: Programs may improve relationship norms, bystander behavior, conflict skills, and recognition of unhealthy relationship patterns, reducing perpetration and some forms of victimization.
edges.summary: Teen dating violence prevention programs reduce overall dating violence outcomes on average, though effects differ by violence subtype and program design.
edges.caveats: Evidence is stronger for physical violence and perpetration-related outcomes than for sexual violence outcomes. Programs vary widely in intensity, setting, and follow-up duration.

evidence.citation: Piolanti A and Foran HM 2022 JAMA Pediatr
evidence.notes: Efficacy of Interventions to Prevent Physical and Sexual Dating Violence Among Adolescents: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

evidence.citation: Foshee VA et al 1998 Am J Public Health
evidence.notes: An evaluation of Safe Dates, an adolescent dating violence prevention program.

evidence.citation: Peskin MF et al 2019 Am J Public Health
evidence.notes: Adolescent Dating Violence Prevention Program for Early Adolescents: The Me & You Randomized Controlled Trial, 2014-2015.
